coupled_sources.reason: a reservation resolves to a job id, and server_compute.c records that the ledger and the launch were co-located after a ledger across a boundary from the launch left paid-for jobs that nothing could replay

families.name: economizer_state
families.doc: the economizer's per-conversation reducer state. Chosen as the first family because it has exactly one production caller, so it proved the boundary without a wide cutover.

families.name: git_ownership
families.doc: branch ownership for the MCP git flows. Rows say which session owns which branch, so concurrent local sessions do not stomp on each other.
families.client_doc: A failure returns -1, never "no owner". branch_own_check() reads a negative as "no enforcement" and allows the operation, which is what it has always done without a database, whereas a fabricated 0 would assert the branch is unowned and let a caller take one somebody else holds.

families.name: conversation
families.doc: per-conversation context, clarifications and working memory.
families.covers: conv_context, clarify, payload_rewrite_state, user_memory, wm, windows

families.name: agent_work
families.doc: queued agent work: logs, coordination jobs and the cron that drives them.
families.client_doc: Background work queues: the cognify queue's claim/mark bookkeeping is machine-local runtime state, which is why it is DB1's even when the memory it points at lives in DB2.

families.name: delegation
families.doc: delegation spawns, reservations, checkpoints and the agent_jobs ledger they reserve against. These move as ONE unit: a reservation resolves to a job id, and server_compute.c records that the ledger and the launch were deliberately co-located because a ledger across a boundary from the launch left paid-for jobs that nothing could replay. Splitting them across families would restore exactly that topology one migration at a time.

families.name: sessions
families.doc: server and webchat session rows: who is talking, when they last spoke, and what the conversation was called.

families.name: runtime
families.doc: machine-local runtime state: caches, this box's operator and clones, the model catalogue it fetched, and the snapshots it took.
families.covers: caches, decisions, env, fsnap, local_operator, mcp_osv_cache, model_catalog, model_pricing, project_clones, runtime_state, tool_local_availability, web_page_cache, working_profile_local

families.name: telemetry
families.doc: what the system spent and what it noticed: token and cost ledgers, guardrail and interaction events, eval results and diagnoses.
families.covers: cost_fold, diagnose, eval, guardrail_events, interaction_events, token_audit

families.name: guardrail_state
families.doc: per-session guardrail state: the hook's view of a session, stored as a scalar row plus five child tables and read back as one nested struct.

families.name: ensemble
families.doc: multi-agent ensemble runs: one table holding a run's state, plus the template interpretation and prompt building that only the run itself uses. Template files are resolved from roots the caller names.

families.name: workflow
families.doc: the workflow engine's plans, traces, pipelines and bindings -- everything the engine stores that no multi-call transaction spans.

families.name: roundtable
families.doc: roundtable pipeline runs, passes, attempts and gates: the review pipeline's own state machine, split from workflow because one family's generated client cannot hold both.

families.name: identity
families.doc: the appliance's first-user remote-client grant: the enrollment bearer, the certificate it binds to, and the tier that grant carries.

families.name: checkpoints
families.doc: session checkpoint rows: a label, the session it belongs to and the snapshot it captured.

families.name: jti_replay
families.doc: single-use JTI replay windows for the identity and management token paths. Reserved: these entry points are not named db1_, which the catalog requires, and each has a _consume_for_test twin that a production wire has no place for.

families.name: lifecycle
families.doc: work-item state and its audit log. Split from workflow because wfe_engine.c wraps sixteen of these writes in two transactions it opens and commits across separate calls, which is a redesign of that engine's write path rather than a wire question.

families.name: mgmt_jwks
families.doc: the management-JWKS cache row: the envelope the server verified, when it is valid for, and the digests that pin it. Digests cross as hex because the wire has no bytes.

families.name: mgmt_nonce
families.doc: management challenge nonces and the revocation high-water mark: issued once, consumed once, and the counter that stops a replayed status report rolling the server backwards.

families.name: pki
families.doc: the client-certificate roster and the mTLS ramp: which certificates exist, when each was last presented, and how far the ramp from optional to required has come.
